rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Youth and enslaved Muslims faced severe pressure from parents and masters, raising doubts about the Qur’an and the Prophet that needed answering to encourage the weak.
rows.anchor: the youth and the slaves were passing through very severe trials from their fathers and masters respectively during the course of revelation of this sūrah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah admonishes forceful oppressors who mistake God’s reprieve for triumph.
rows.anchor: who had become open and forceful in their oppression by regarding the reprieve granted to them by God as their triumph

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oppressed believers should be ready to migrate for truth; God’s earth has safe havens and ample provisions, and He will care for those who migrate for His cause.
rows.anchor: Neither is God’s earth devoid of safe havens nor is there any decrease in His treasure of provisions

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous sūrah only hints at opposition from the People of the Book, while this sūrah depicts it openly and guides Muslims in responding to them.
rows.anchor: In the previous sūrah, some indications are found of the opposition of the People of the Book

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 1–7 teach that those who follow truth will be tested, as an established divine practice that distinguishes believers from hypocrites.
rows.anchor: people who tread the path of the truth will necessarily be tried and tested. This is an established practice of God. It distinguishes a believer from a hypocrite

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those granted respite should know they cannot escape God’s grasp.
rows.anchor: people today who have been granted respite should bear in mind that they cannot escape from God’s grasp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers enduring injustice for their faith will receive a reward exceeding the hardships they suffer.
rows.anchor: they will be rewarded much more than the troubles they are passing through for the cause of faith

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience to parents and elders is bounded by obedience to God; they are obeyed only while remaining subordinate to Him.
rows.anchor: The bounds and limits of obedience to the parents and the elders are explained: they should be obeyed while remaining subservient to God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children must refuse their parents if they demand disobedience to God.
rows.anchor: if the parents of some children demand that they be disobedient to God, then they should not comply with them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in retribution entails glorifying God in the morning, evening, at ẓuhr, and at ʿaṣr.
rows.anchor: the consequence of this belief is that they should only glorify God by morning and evening

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase praising God in the heavens and earth is parenthetical between the specified times of glorification and serves as a reminder and warning.
rows.anchor: form a parenthetical sentence in between the times of glorifying God. It is meant to remind and warn people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All parts of the heavens and earth praise God, so those who worship others are out of harmony with the universe, while those who praise God are in harmony with it.
rows.anchor: every part of the heavens and the earth are singing His praises

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording also conveys aloofness: those who fail to glorify God should not imagine that praise is scarce, since the universe resounds with it.
rows.anchor: the unfortunate people who are not glorifying God and singing His praises should not think that there is a dearth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed times coincide with major signs such as night turning to day, day to night, sunset, and nightfall, which should move reflective people to remember God.
rows.anchor: the times which God has specified for expressing His glorification and praise are the ones in which a great sign appears

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If such transformations do not stir someone to remember God, Islahi calls that person spiritually dull.
rows.anchor: If this does not move a person, then it means he is a dull animal

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajr and ẓuhr are explicit; reading tumsūn as ʿaṣr and maghrib and ʿashiyyan as ʿishāʾ would include all prayer times.
rows.anchor: The prayers of fajr and ẓuhr are very clearly mentioned in these verses

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAshiyyan can denote the time of zawāl or the interval between maghrib and ʿishāʾ, so taking it to indicate ʿishāʾ is reasonable.
rows.anchor: The word اًّیِشَع can be applied both to the time of zawāl (time of sun’s descent) and to the time between maghrib and ‘ishā’

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section II orders arguments for the Hereafter and monotheism: the Hereafter gives this world meaning, and monotheism makes divine judgment meaningful because no intercessor can obstruct God’s impartial justice.
rows.anchor: In the succeeding verses, arguments to substantiate the Hereafter and monotheism are mentioned in an appropriate order

none: Continuation of Qur’anic text and translation only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links this argument to 36:77–78, where a human who forgets his own creation mocks the possibility of reviving decayed bones.
rows.anchor: Qur’ān in the following words:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made spouses from the same human species for comfort and placed love and sympathy between them as signs for reflection.
rows.anchor: God created from His species his spouse so that he may obtain comfort from her and for this purpose placed love and sympathy among them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first sign is that everything is created in pairs whose members complement one another; this implies that the world’s pair is the Hereafter, with which this world becomes meaningful.
rows.anchor: God has created everything in pairs in this universe and each member of a pair complements its counterpart

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second sign is the Creator’s mercy: He made spouses of the same species and joined them through love and sympathy, so they live as two bodies with one soul.
rows.anchor: our creator is very merciful and affectionate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third sign is the harmony and accord among opposing elements of the universe, which converge to fulfill a higher objective.
rows.anchor: there exists great harmony in the opposing elements of this universe and an amazing accord to come together to fulfill a higher objective

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth sign rejects a self-originating universe: harmony among opposites shows that a powerful, wise being governs the system.
rows.anchor: people who think that this universe was created of its own accord are foolish

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the distance between the heavens and earth, their deep relationship and shared purpose show that one powerful, wise Creator governs them, not separate creators or forces.
rows.anchor: hidden in the multiplicity found in this universe is unity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different nations, languages, accents, and colors likewise come from one Creator; the diversity reflects creative skill, with every person distinct in voice, color, height, and features.
rows.anchor: It is merely the profound nature of His creative skill that He has created every single person in a different mold with a different voice

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truly knowledgeable reflect on the universe, discern unity in multiplicity and accord in discord, infer God’s power, wisdom, and purpose, and recognize that Judgment must bring reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: the real knowledgeable are those who reflect on this universe and through this reflection observe unity in multiplicity and accord in discord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Differences of language and color should not be grounds for discrimination or division; all people are God’s creatures and should live under His governance.
rows.anchor: the difference in the language and colour among people should not be made the basis of discrimination between them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Discriminating among people by color and creed attacks the unity of the universe and is, in Qur’anic terms, polytheism and spreading disorder on earth.
rows.anchor: in the terms of the Qur’ān is polytheism and spreading disorder in the land
